title: Celebrations in Belgrade after Serbian leader Vučić admits election defeat. #BBCNews

author: BBC News
description:
Serbia's long-standing leader Aleksandar Vučić has admitted defeat to the student-led protest movement in snap parliamentary elections. “I is clear that we have lost these elections," the right-wing populist leader said as he conceded.

Preliminary figures provided by Serbia's election commission indicated a record high turnout, which commentators had suggested would favour the student movement.

Vučić had called the snap elections after two years of protests triggered by the 2024 collapse of a train station canopy in the city of Novi Sad, which killed 16 and was seen as emblematic of corruption and negligence in Serbia.

He made his announcement at the headquarters of his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in the capital Belgrade.
There were celebrations on the streets of the city, with people dancing and chanting "victory", cars honking, and fireworks set off. "Serbia is free," one student told the BBC. "It's a miracle."

Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor are among the actors thought to be taking part in final auditions to play James Bond, according to reports.

Screen tests are said to be taking place this weekend, according to the Hollywood Reporter, with between three and five actors understood to have reached the last stages of the process.

The finalists are said to be taking part in auditions with three components - stunts, camera presence and dialogue.

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he would welcome an "honest discussion" about the prospect of returning to free movement between the UK and European Union.

In an interview with the Sunday Times political editor Ben Riley-Smith, he said a new relationship with Brussels could also include full EU membership or joining the single market.

Ben is in the studio to talk about what the PM told him, along with Laura, Paddy and Joe Pike.

description:
Brazilians are voting to choose their next president in a closely fought run-off election.
 
The choice is between incumbent left-wing leader Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro.
 
It is the second round of voting after Bolsonaro won the first round earlier this month - beating President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known widely as Lula.
 
Bolsonaro told reporters on Sunday that the "time has come for real change", while Lula was pictured greeting supporters outside a polling station.

description:
Storm Boelo has brought in flooding, travel disruption, and power cuts across the UK.

On the railways, people are being told not to certain areas.

In Scotland, Network Rail said trees have fallen onto lines at "numerous locations", while many ferry services have also been suspended.

Power cuts have hit tens of thousands of properties across England, Scotland and the island of Ireland, and amber warnings remain in place.

description:
Nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands people took part in another day of protests across France.
 
After a day of largely peaceful demonstrations, clashes occurred late on Saturday with police firing tear gas and water cannons to disperse protestors in a number of cities including Paris.
 
The interior ministry said an estimated 410,000 people protested on Saturday, while the unions put the number at about 800,000.
 
Hundreds of people have been jailed for vandalism, arson and looting after the protests over the cost of living and poor school conditions descended into chaos.

author: BBC News
description:
Are Hasan Piker’s controversial views a help or a hindrance for the Democrats this midterms?

He’s arguably America’s most high-profile left-wing influencer but he’s not loved by all Democrats. He made his name streaming on Twitch and helped propel Abdul El-Sayed as the Democrat candidate in Michigan for the state’s all important Senate seat. Justin’s been speaking to Hasan Piker about comments he’s made in the past which are now being used by Republicans on the campaign trail.

And with less than two weeks to go, the race for the state’s open seat is close, and could help decide who controls the US Senate. Sarah’s there and joins Justin and Marianna to discuss the final debate between the Democratic and Republican candidates in Michigan, and whether Democrats can win back voters who backed Donald Trump in 2024.
